newsitem.title: USA: Study clears way for new use of bomb test site.
newsitem.headline: Study clears way for new use of bomb test site.

text.p: A two-year study cleared the way for the Energy Department to expand use of its bomb testing site in Nevada for energy and environmental research, the Energy Department said Tuesday.
The department's study analysed the impact that current and planned defence and civilian experiments might have on the environment around the 1,350 square mile Nevada test site.
The Energy Department plans to use the site for scientific tests to ensure the safety and reliability of the U.S. nuclear stockpile, without any explosions.
It might build a solar power tower or dish systems on the land to generate up to 1,000 megawatts of electricity.

The site could also be used for simulating spills of toxic chemicals, training people to respond to commercial chemical and gaseous accidents, developing technologies for cleaning up hazardous wastes, and finding ways to restore wildlife habitats.
